questions.q: What real detail about `raw_payments.amount` makes a macro worth writing here?
options: It's stored in a different currency per row
It's stored as a text string that needs parsing
It's sometimes null and needs a default value
It's stored in cents, not dollars, and every money-displaying model needs the same conversion
questions.explain: raw_payments.amount is in cents in the real jaffle_shop data (2691 means $26.91) — a conversion every money-touching model needs identically.

options: `{% macro cents_to_dollars(column_name, decimal_places=2) %} round({{ column_name }} / 100.0, {{ decimal_places }}) {% endmacro %}`
`def cents_to_dollars(column_name): return column_name / 100`
`{{ macro cents_to_dollars }} ... {{ end }}`
`CREATE FUNCTION cents_to_dollars(amount) RETURNS amount/100`
questions.explain: {% macro %} / {% endmacro %} is the real Jinja syntax; decimal_places=2 gives that argument a default.

questions.q: Where is `cents_to_dollars()` called in this lesson, and why there specifically?
options: In the Power BI measure, so dbt never has to touch it
It isn't called anywhere yet — that's left for Lesson 11
In `fct_orders`, because that's the final model
In `stg_jaffle_shop__payments`, so every downstream model already receives dollars, not cents
questions.explain: Applying the conversion as early as possible, in staging, means fct_orders and everything after it already work in dollars.

questions.q: What does `{{ cents_to_dollars('amount') }}` compile down to?
options: `round(amount / 100.0, 2)`
A call to a Python function at query time
Nothing — it has to be called with both arguments every time
`amount * 100`
questions.explain: The macro's rendered text is plain SQL — no leftover Jinja syntax in the compiled model.

questions.q: Why is this specific conversion a good candidate for a macro, by this project's own rule?
options: Because any calculation involving division must be a macro
Because dbt requires all column transformations to be macros
Because it makes the compiled SQL shorter
The same logic is needed by more than one model, and it's a single business rule that should have exactly one place to change
questions.explain: The rule from the project's own macros lesson: write a macro when logic repeats across models or represents one rule that should have one place to change.
